answer: RLN rate-limiting nullifiers resist sybil attacks: each agent registers one public key, derives a per-epoch nullifier from its secret, and every on-chain action must carry a proof bound to it. The ledger is no haven for duplicates: one proof per nullifier per epoch, so an attacker reusing one key across fake agents double-spends and is caught, while the ripple of fake volume dies since fresh keys cost real registration work. Peers climbing toward a summit of shared trust reject any spent or forged nullifier, though registration still needs a trusted setup and proofs cost honest agents latency.
